However, some fundamental problems have not been properly addressed such as maximum safe operating voltages and critical dimensions required at small separations between different types of materials. Specimens for examination at electrode separations from 500 nm to 25 /spl mu/m have been made with different electrode configurations, such as flat to flat, flat to point and point to point. All the tests were made in air, at differing pressures and finally using SF/sub 6/.

articleTitle: Protection of gas-insulated substations including corona and ohmic losses
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The present paper discusses the simulation of a power transmission system, where a ZnO arrester is connected either at the power cable/GIS junction or across the transformer, whilst also considering the effect of line and cable losses. The line losses are corona losses due to corona discharges and ohmic losses in conductors and earth return paths. The cable loss is ohmic loss due to the skin effect. The line and cable are simulated by dividing them into a number of equal sections and each section is represented by a lossless line in cascade connection with a discrete element network to simulate the losses within the section. Computed lightning overvoltage waveshapes at the power cable/GIS junction and across the transformer with and without the arrester are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Statistical breakdown behavior of N/sub 2/-SF/sub 6/ gas mixtures under LI stress
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The statistical scattering of breakdown voltage in pure sulfur hexafluoride (SF/sub 6/) and mixtures with nitrogen (N/sub 2/) in case of quasi uniform fields under lightning impulse (LI) stress was investigated under positive polarity in the pressure range between 0.54 MPa for pure SF/sub 6/ up to 1.42 MPa for the mixture with 1% SF/sub 6/ content. The basic requirement for these investigations was to get the same dielectric strength with all N/sub 2/-SF/sub 6/ gas mixtures compared to pure SF/sub 6/. First conclusions concerning the statistical breakdown behavior of N/sub 2/-SF/sub 6/ gas mixtures are drawn.

articleTitle: High order mode waves excited in GIS
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: UHF signal measurement based on the high order mode waves, is an important tool for the partial discharge detection in GIS (gas insulated substation). In this paper, the high order mode wave excitation and propagation are discussed. From experimental results, some properties are derived: the velocity of the high order mode waves (TE and TM modes) is less than the TEM mode velocity; the high order mode wave in GIS is dependent on the GIS geometry and on the source of excitation; and the resonant cavity is important for the high order mode signal detection.

articleTitle: The influence of a conducting particle on a spacer on the insulation properties in SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ mixtures
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The flashover behaviour of a spacer sample with a conducting particle on the surface was investigated for several SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ mixtures with SF/sub 6/ content up to 30%. LI 1.2/50 /spl mu/s and AC 50 Hz were used to stress the setup. The gas pressure ranged from 100 to 600 kPa. The particle was 0.25 mm in diameter with a length of 2 to 8.5 mm. The spacer sample was 25 mm in diameter and 45 mm in length and made out of epoxy resin filled with Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/. The results of the investigations show the influence of the particle length and the gas pressure on the flashover voltage for various SF/sub 6/ contents of the mixtures.

articleTitle: DC and AC breakdown voltage behavior of high voltage multi-layer encapsulated coils
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The trend in designing small and lightweight miniaturized high voltage electric and electronic equipments has increased over the last two decades. This was generally achieved by using solid potting and multi-layer insulation systems with reduced size of insulation layers and by using fine gauge magnet wires. Further, PET thermoplastic encapsulation of coils and electronic devices has also been used for electrical insulation, heat dissipation and physical protection of the encapsulated devices from harsh environmental operating conditions. This paper presents the results of breakdown tests on units of high voltage multi-layer encapsulated coils at DC and AC voltages. The effect of the temperature and moisture absorption on the breakdown is also investigated. The breakdown were presented by Weibull statistical distribution.

articleTitle: Mechanical performance of GRP rods used in nonceramic insulators after exposure to acid attack
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The results of the mechanical performance evaluation of five types of GRP rods used in NCI are presented. The fractographic characteristics of the rods after exposure to oxalic, nitric and sulfuric acid solutions are also presented. No evidence is found to conclude that the sole action of the acids induce transverse cracking of the rods in a planar mode. Extensive fiber pullout was observed during the mechanical test. The tested rods showed a more marked reduction in their mechanical strength after nitric acid attack. The transverse cracking of the rods in a planar mode which is characteristic of the brittle fracture is found to be dependent on the simultaneous action of mechanical and chemical stresses.

articleTitle: A study of memory effect of partial discharges
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: From the computed conditional pulse amplitude and phase distributions it is shown that, as the gap spacing is reduced, the charging of a dielectric surface affects the corona pulse-time distribution which becomes significant at lower gap spacings. Most probable values are found to be the best statistical indicators for interpreting the results.

articleTitle: Lightning protection system to the Indian satellite launch pad
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Any satellite launch mission forms a complex and expensive process. Intensive care and precautions are to be taken for a safe and successful launch. Also, the satellite launch system forms a tall structure standing on a plane terrain. As a result, a lightning strike rate to it becomes more probable. Therefore, extensive care needs to be taken in shielding the launch system against natural lightning. Lightning protection systems built with differing principles have been in use at different launch centers throughout the world. This paper describes the lightning protection system that has been installed at the SHAR Indian satellite launch center.

articleTitle: Practical applications for the machine intelligent partial discharge disturbing pulse suppression system NeuroTEK II
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) measurements, especially for on-site applications, have the problem that PD information is superimposed with electromagnetic disturbances. To solve this problem, a fast machine intelligent signal recognition system for the suppression of disturbing pulses was developed. This system distinguishes between PD and pulse shaped noise by referring to the time-resolved signal shape in real-time using a neural network hardware in a PC host. In this paper, practical applications for the disturbance pulse suppression are presented. Therefore measurements with a laboratory test set-up and artificial PD sources as well as results from an on-site measurement in gas insulated switchgear (GIS) were performed. Another application is the disturbance free determination of a PD fault location on-site.

articleTitle: Investigation on electrical aging of thin polypropylene films for power capacitors by means of thermally stimulated depolarisation currents (TSC)
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Electrical aging of polymer materials in different geometries have been the subject of many investigations. Aging of polypropylene films for power capacitors is of interest mainly with respect to the lifetime. Dielectric films in capacitors are stressed by high electrical fields, high temperatures and chemicals. For reducing the electrical field stress in gaseous voids, inevitable during manufacturing, capacitors are impregnated with fluids. Interactions with the fluids cannot be excluded. It can be supposed that the temperature and the level of the electric field influence the build-up of space charges. The method of thermally stimulated currents of depolarisation (TSC) allows indication of changes in space charges build-up by electrical stress. By this method, influences of temperature, electrical field stress and the surface treatment of the films can be elaborated.

articleTitle: Skin and Ferranti effects of ZnO internal current to very fast transient current
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Response characteristics of a ZnO element generally used for surge arresters against very fast transients are hardly known. They have not only nonlinear resistance characteristics but also dielectric ones. The authors have developed an analytical digital program to study internal resistive and capacitive currents of the element to very fast transient current, based on Maxwell equations. And moreover, its equivalent circuit has been developed. This paper shows not only the outline of theory and equivalent circuit, but also that of skin and Ferranti effects on ZnO internal currents.

articleTitle: On the significance of PD measurements in liquids
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper presents experimental data and calculations concerning the measurement of partial discharges (PDs) in mineral oil. The influence of the RLC measuring impedance is studied. The investigations were done using either signals of simple shapes or real PD signals. PDs were produced with a point-plane gap in air and in mineral oil. The discharge currents in air are integrated by the usual RLC whereas in mineral oil the charge is strongly underestimated.

articleTitle: Dielectric strength of short contact gaps in a vacuum interrupter after switching operations
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The electric strength of a vacuum gap of a given geometry and dimensions is strongly dependent on the state of the contact surface. The aim of this work is to investigate and compare breakdown voltages of the vacuum interrupter cold gap with CuCr contacts for selected switching operations. Additionally, the aim of this research is to broaden known measurement results of late restrike voltages with new data.

articleTitle: A method for field verification of the precision class of inductive voltage transformers
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: It is shown here that the precision class of an IVT-inductive voltage transformer-can be verified in the field, using the results obtained in the usual tests of no-load loss and current, short circuit and winding ohmic resistances, performed with common meters. A graphic diagram-the Mollinger and Gewecke diagram-is employed together with the results of an accuracy test previously carried out in order to determine the exact value of the winding turns relation and of the primary winding dispersion reactance. These values are used to calculate phase and magnitude errors, that must obey standards and must lie between definite limits, defined by the precision class of the instrument. Some commercial IVTs were tested in order to check the validation of the procedure. The errors were compared with the ones obtained with the Shering-Alberti method (CA bridge and comparison with standard IVT).

articleTitle: Field experience with non-ceramic hollow-core insulators
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper reports on field experience with AC-energized hollow-core polymeric insulators. The paper presents the leakage current performance and the hydrophobicity status of the insulators. For the purpose of reference, a hollow-core insulator made of porcelain is also included in this paper. The insulators were mounted in both an upright as well as an inclined position. Also, the specific creepage paths of the insulators were relatively low, in the order of 12.4 to 14.7 mm/kV only. The presented results refer to a period of four years. The obtained results show that there is a clear difference in the performance between the upright and the inclined insulators. The inclined insulator has somewhat higher leakage currents, In addition, the hydrophobicity is lower on the underside of the inclined insulator.

articleTitle: Compensation of step response "creeping" of a damped capacitor divider for switching impulses
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The subject of "creeping" dividers is still a practical problem in any high-voltage laboratory. This paper describes a procedure that may be used to correct the step response creeping of a damped capacitor divider due to frequency dependence of the high voltage capacitor. This involves several steps, starting from the initial step response measurement, then, estimation of the values of compensating components, confirmation of the compensated step response using a circuit emulation program, and the final response measurement/component refinement and any necessary iteration.

articleTitle: Improving the failure detection in the lightning impulse test of low inductance air core reactors
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper discusses the lightning impulse test of air core reactors concerning the influence of the earthing resistor. The results of lightning impulse tests done in a 421 /spl mu/H air core reactor are presented and discussed regarding the failure detection. Suggestions for improving the insulation failure detection are given.

articleTitle: A 300 V mercury switch pulse generator with 70 psec risetime for investigation of UHF PD signal transmission in GIS
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: A mercury switch pulse generator for the purpose of high frequency characterization of gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is presented. The compact device is well matched to 50 /spl Omega/ and operates with a DC voltage of 300 V. It consists of a charged cable, a fast mercury switch relay and supporting passive elements. With this combination, a 150 V pulse may be applied to a GIS partial discharge (PD) sensor with a 70 ps rise time and a 50 ns pulse length, having a maximum repetition rate of more than 100 Hz. The robust device is lightweight and easy to handle. Due to its modular design, it may be directly connected to a GIS PD sensor. It may be used for the simulation of PD discharges in GIS, for impulse propagation speed measurements and for the sensitivity check of GIS PD sensors together with UHF PD measurement systems.

articleTitle: Design of a novel oil tester calibrator based on capacitive dividing mechanisms
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high voltage (HV) measuring instrument designed to calibrate oil insulation testers. Two parts were included: the calibrator block; and the data processing and display unit. It overcomes the difficulties of measuring high voltage in a small enclosure. The designed instrument can be used for any other HV measurements, especially within small enclosures.

articleTitle: Reference standard digital recorder with 200 MS/s-12 bit for HV impulse tests
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper describes the hardware of a new generation of digital recorders, designed and optimized to fulfil all requirements for measuring of full or chopped lightning, switching and current impulses according to all applicable standards. Such digital recorders are required for Accredited Laboratories and National Metrological Laboratories. The results of the official calibration of the first digital recorder type TR-AS 200-12 performed by the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Braunschweig are shown. This digital recorder is available now as Reference Standard of Measurement in our DKD Calibration Laboratory for electrical impulse parameter. The technical data and software properties are described.

articleTitle: Experimental study on factors affecting the probability distribution of discharge striking points
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Several factors affecting the probability distribution of discharge striking points have been studied by contrast test. There exists a hierarchy relationship between the probability distribution of discharge striking points and the breakdown voltage, the breakdown time and the development of head-on discharge. The distribution is influenced by geometric shape of objective, ground resistance, geometric striking distance, and so on. The study deepens the knowledge of the physical process of the selection of lightning striking points.

articleTitle: A new dielectric type test procedure for live working tools
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: We present a new dielectric test procedure that guarantees a correct design of the internal insulation of tools used for the maintenance of electrical installations, with special attention to the limits of applicability in terms of nominal voltages of installations. This test procedure was laid down to ensure relevance regarding this type of failure, simplicity of the required test facilities and coherence with the practices of IEC TC 78.

articleTitle: Effect of concurrent ELF electric and magnetic fields on induced current density in biological model in the vicinity of the ground
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In this paper the characteristics of total current density in a homogeneous prolate spheroid model of biological object exposed to 60 Hz electric and magnetic fields (electric field: 1 kV/m, magnetic field: 1/spl mu/T) have been discussed in consideration of phase difference between vertical electric field and horizontal magnetic field. The current density induced by the electric field is calculated using the finite element method.

articleTitle: Empirical model of a high voltage insulator under nonuniform pollution
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Experimental results on the influence of the dry zone length and its position, with respect to the electrodes, on the leakage current and the arc length are used to determine an empirical model. The tests are conducted on a plane experimental model under AC voltage. Two configurations of the pollution layer are considered: (i) at the high voltage electrode side; and (ii) at the ground electrode side. Different conductivities of the wet layer are used. By adopting some simplified assumptions some of which being based on the experimental results, the authors propose a simple empirical model. This latter gives the expression of the whole impedance between the electrodes, from which they deduce the transferred voltage on the dry zone, whatever the configuration of the pollution. The obtained results show that the empirical model gives very correct results in the case of a linear system. Beyond this latter, the model is convenient no longer because of the probable decrease of the apparent impedance of the dry zone when the system becomes critical.

articleTitle: Calibration system and uncertainty budget for instrument transformers with digital output
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper describes the reference system employed during calibration of instrument transformers with digital output. The reference system can be used for calibration of both current and voltage transformers by changing the references. The uncertainties associated with the calibrations of current transformers are evaluated and typical values are presented, including the established pool of variances for this calibration. This leads to a total uncertainty for transducer calibration of the same order of magnitude as that of analogue bridge calibrations in an industrial environment for traditional instrument transformers.

articleTitle: Study of the breakdown voltage of the air in high altitudes, applying lightning impulses (1.2/50 /spl mu/s) under conditions of controlled humidity and temperature
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Air as insulating material has been studied a lot. However, for altitudes greater than 2000 meters above sea level, not many projects have been accomplished. The international standard establishes correction factors for atmospheric conditions that have not yet been studied for low-pressure conditions. This article presents a study of the air breakdown at the altitude of Santafe de Bogota (2540 m above sea level) applying lightning impulse voltages (LIV: 1.2/50 /spl mu/s) for the two polarities and controlling humidity and temperature with the objective of determining the influence of the atmospheric conditions in the behavior of air as insulation at high altitudes.

articleTitle: Comparison of electrical environmental characteristics of different EHV transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The present paper reports the analysis results by comparison of characteristics of electrical environment between different EHV transmission lines such as AN (audible noise), RI (radio interference), TVI (television interference), EMF (electromagnetic fields). In Korea, transmission lines with nominal voltage of 765 kV have been constructed since 1996, and Hungary energized a 750 kV line in 1978. However both EHV transmission lines have different line configurations. Korea is a prime example of the first double circuit 765 kV line in the world and Hungary has been operating one of the single circuit 750 kV.

articleTitle: Relevance of the charging period to the dielectric response based diagnosis of PE/XLPE cables
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The measurement of the so-called dielectric response is one of the approaches for nondestructive insulation diagnosis. In the frequency domain the dielectric response can be obtained by capacitance and dissipation factor measurements, in time domain by depolarisation and polarisation current or recovery voltage measurements. The paper presents dielectric response measurements of different aged and unaged XLPE-insulated medium voltage cables in dependence of the required charging period prior to the time domain measurement. Furthermore, the results are compared to results of destructive test methods.

articleTitle: Internal degradation of polymer housed metal oxide surge arresters in very humid ambient conditions
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: A total of 19 new, polymer housed metal oxide surge arresters of seven different types were tested in a 25-month moisture ingress test series in very humid ambient conditions at Tampere University of Technology (TUT). Internal degradation due to moisture ingress in the different arrester types during the test with respect to the internal structure of arresters is reported. Only three of the seven arrester types tested showed good performance throughout the test. These arrester types had a housing molded directly on the arrester body. Most of the other arresters failed during the test or immediately after the test under an AC voltage stress. The trend of the internal leakage current was found to be heavily dependent on the internal structure of an arrester.

articleTitle: Calculation of the electrostatic force acting on axisymmetric objects in nonuniform electric fields
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper presents the evaluation of the resultant force acting on an axisymmetric body in an electrostatic field. The objects can be either dielectrics or conductors, charged or uncharged. Basically, the computation is carried out by linking the Maxwell stress tensor to a 2D field calculation program. The main purpose of the work is to create a numerical tool for calculating forces on dielectric and metallic particles in the presence of nonuniform electric fields. As a demonstration, two examples are presented in the paper. One of them, the force on a charged dielectric sphere due to a point charge external to the sphere, has an analytical solution and is therefore used to check the validity of the model. The analytical result verified the approach. The other example is an uncharged ellipsoid placed in a rod-plane gap. The force on the ellipsoid is investigated for different positions in the gap and for different choices of dielectric constant.

articleTitle: Development of 1 MV steep-front rectangular-impulse voltage generator
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The basic design and performance of a newly developed 1 MV steep-front rectangular-impulse voltage generator, named "SPARK", are described. Advanced pulsed-power technology and elaborate circuit design enable an ideal rectangular waveform, in which the rise time of the wavefront is shorter than 20 ns and a long flat-topped voltage crest continues up to 10 /spl mu/s, to be generated. By applying this waveform as a test voltage to a model GIS (gas-insulated switchgear) gap, quantitative evaluation of the voltage-time characteristics can be achieved.

articleTitle: Field simulations for high voltage applications
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper is not intended to be a contribution to state the manifold and successful ongoing development and research activities in the framework of numerical field simulations in high voltage applications. It is shown how modern and novel techniques are applied to simulate physical phenomena out of the as classically regarded world of power engineering. Carefully selected examples of technical importance demonstrate the strength of the computation methods chosen. Nowadays, specialised software packages to tackle realistic problems are not exclusively used by highly skilled university researchers; there are various commercial software products on the market.

articleTitle: High-voltage field computation using bi-cubic surface splines
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Integral equation methods are used to compute the electric field stress on high-voltage arrangements. This paper combines the geometric description of surfaces, using bi-cubic spline functions on individual patches, with the boundary element method for calculating three-dimensional electrostatic fields. After the calculation of spline function coefficients from a given geometric design, the electric boundary conditions of electrode and dielectric parts are applied. Numerical integration by means of Gaussian quadrature leads to a linear system of equations, determining the charge density on the surface elements. This solution is used to calculate the potential and field strength on the electrode or insulator contour. The accuracy of the method is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Lightning protection and the physics of discharge
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The way of designing protection systems and of evaluating their exposure to lightning has been improved significantly, mainly during the last 50 years, thanks both to studies in the field and to laboratory research into long air gap breakdown. On the basis of the knowledge acquired, various models for lightning exposure evaluation have been developed, based on the description of the different phases of discharge development. The aim of this paper is to analyse three models in the case of negative lightning which is the most common event, especially in the case of structures not particularly high off the ground.

articleTitle: Design and construction of a PC-based PD detector and locator for HV cables using FPGA
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Rapid development in field programmable gate arrays (FPGA) technology opens up a new opportunity to develop re-configurable real time DSP to reduce disturbances during PD measurements under on-site conditions. This paper applies this technology in the design and construction of a real-time PD detector and locator. The detector and locator consists of analog circuits and digital circuits most of which are programmed into an FPGA chip. Then, the FPGA chip, the analog circuits and digital circuits are fabricated into a PCB that can be inserted into a slot of a PC. The instrument results in a low-cost and high-performance digital PD measuring system.

articleTitle: Effect of ozonized water treatment on electrical breakdown of oxygen-free copper electrodes of a vacuum gap
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: An ozonized water treatment technique was applied to surface treatment of oxygen-free copper electrodes. Breakdown characteristics of the electrodes were measured in a vacuum by applying impulse voltages. Results showed that the breakdown field at the first voltage application was not improved, but the conditioning effect of the gap by repetitive breakdowns was significant. The value of breakdown field after conditioning was around 250 MV/m (for a 0.3-mm gap length). Breakdown fields were lowered to values similar to those of the first voltage application, after the conditioned electrodes were exposed to air for two to three weeks. Reconditioning, however, was achieved rapidly.

articleTitle: Nanosecond forming line based on compact power high-voltage pulse capacitors
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Specific problems regarding high-voltage pulse capacitors for quasi-rectangular nanosecond pulse formation at a low resistive load are discussed. Such a capacitor could be presented as a ladder-circuit which functions as a strip transmission line discharging to a matched load. The capacitor consists of conventional low inductive capacitor sections. The packages of these sections are connected in parallel by means of plate conductors which form the main (longitudinal) inductance of circuit cells. The inductance of the packages (the transverse inductance) affects negatively the shape of the formed pulse. The capacitor construction is improved by making the circuit cells nonuniform. As a result the negative effect of the transverse inductance could be cancelled. Furthermore, the nonuniform capacitor consists of a half number of the cells as compared with the uniform one and provides the same front and tail steepness and flat-top stability. A numerical calculation technique is developed which could be applied for such nonuniform circuit calculation. The experimental results are in very good agreement with the theoretical behavior and demonstrate the following characteristics achieved with compact nonuniform capacitors: pulse length of 30 ns to 1 ms, front steepness of up to 10/sup 13/ A/s, resistive load of 1 to 10 Ohm, charging voltage of up to 200 kV.

articleTitle: Determination of the electrical properties of mixed transformer fluids under thermal ageing
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper deals with some ageing investigations on two insulating fluids which appear to be particularly suitable for the retrofilling of a perchlorethylene based fluid (Transclene) filled transformers. After a description of the ageing procedure some details of the changes in both the dielectrical and electrical behaviour are described. A comparison of the measured values with the predetermination of the relevant standards and the consequences for the use of the insulation liquid mixture are presented.

articleTitle: Corona stabilisation in SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ mixtures under VFT stress
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper mainly deals with the calculation of the corona radius of prebreakdown phenomena of SF/sub 6/ and SF/sub 6//N/sub 2/ gas mixtures in a pressure range from 0.1 MPa to 0.8 MPa for inhomogeneous field configuration under very fast transient voltage stress (VFT).

articleTitle: Outage of a HVDC converter station caused by discharges and AC-flashovers and possible improvements
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The authors examine how, after seven years of operation, in summertime, during bad weather conditions, the most serious flashover occured at a Chinese HVDC convertor station. Three sets of capacitive voltage transformers in the AC yard suffered flashover with damage of some of the sections and one set of capacitive voltage divider experienced a partial discharge even inside the AC yard. Additionally there was a flashover on the noise capacitor in the DC yard. Consequently one DC protection and 5 AC protections activated. A fault analysis is made according to the site investigations and recordings of the monitoring system of the station. Some preventive measures are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Application of FWT (fast wavelet transform) for auto-detection system of partial discharge in power cables
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Conclusively, the statistic results of the data of partial discharges and noise signals transformed by employing FWT (fast wavelet transform) revealed the characteristics of the waveforms in time-frequency space. The authors effectively succeeded to obtain those data that show them the distinguished properties. The significance of this analysis is that they can observe not only the frequency distribution of the spectrum, but also the time distribution of it at the same time. They expect that it will lead a neural network (NN) system to executing the identification or partial discharges in underground power CV cables. The results in employing the NN system with FWT show some aspects that the FWT will be the best method for waveform pattern recognition.

articleTitle: Hazard for electronic equipment near to transmission line struck by lightning
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper deals with analysis of magnetic field due to lightning current flowing along the conductors of transmission line. It is shown that the boundary of high magnetic field may achieve the distance of some tens meters from the line. This effect should be taken into account in the case of neigbouring structures equipped with sensitive electronic systems.

articleTitle: Experimental studies on the mitigation of chance outages in GIS due to conducting particles
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Gas insulated substations (GIS) operable at medium voltages have been in use for some time. In view of their compactness, GIS possess a high degree of reliability of operation in power utility systems. Among the more important problem areas concerning GIS is the adverse effect of metallic particle contamination of the gas medium. In order to be able to improve the operation of GIS in the inevitable presence of particles, a novel method by which the particles are passivated has been suggested. Studies have been conducted to obtain optimal value of conductivity of the coating material to have a better performance.

articleTitle: Test circuits and diagnosis methods of HV SF6 and minimum-oil circuit breakers at capacitive currents switching
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper presents test circuits and measurements for overvoltage determination on capacitive currents switching when disconnecting single capacitor banks and overhead lines and experimental results in a high power laboratory (HPL) and a power network obtained using high voltage SF/sub 6/ and minimum-oil circuit-breakers. Also, the paper presents diagnosis methods for switching process behaviour of SF/sub 6/ circuit-breakers using no-load dielectric strength characteristics.

articleTitle: Comparative accelerated ageing test to assess the sealing performance of composite surge arresters and insulators
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Good end-seal performance against moisture and/or water ingress contributes significantly to the long-term performance of polymeric housed surge arresters and composite insulators that contain interfaces. A thermal cycling immersion test between -20/spl deg/C to +85/spl deg/C in a liquid rather than in air has been used to investigate the comparative behaviour of a wide range of devices. Fast transitions between both temperatures result in considerably higher thermal mechanical stress than most standards recommend. Rapid expansion and retraction of the devices tested formed the basis of this comparative accelerated ageing test. This paper presents some of the comparative results obtained with respectively 5 weeks and 10 weeks thermal cycling testing of a range of 11 kV and 33 kV polymeric surge arresters and 10 weeks thermal cycling of a range of 66 kV suspension composite insulators.

articleTitle: Characteristics of impulse corona discharge current in an electrode system wire-cylinder
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In this work the results of measurements of corona discharge currents of short duration positive polarity impulses in a wire-cylinder coaxial electrode system are presented. The aim of these measurements is to determine the initial data for a physical-mathematical model of the impulse corona discharge in air which are necessary for optimisation of the parameters of the installations for cleaning gases from harmful impurities. The oscillograms of discharge current were obtained for different voltage magnitudes in the range from 15 up to 35 kV for the voltage impulses shape close to the rectangular form with about 150 ns impulse duration. The quantitative data of current measurements expose characteristic features of current-voltage dependencies for impulse corona discharge, which should be taking into account when a physical-mathematical model of the discharge is being developed and the installations are designed.

articleTitle: The heating and the rate of prolongation of the channel of a very long-spark
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The process of the heating of heavy particles in the discharge channel of a long spark is analysed in order to derive the relation of the rates of this process in the case of the positive and of the negative space charge in the surroundings of the channel. A special attention is paid to the combined acting of the one-step and two-step mechanism of ionisation of the plasma. There are discussed the causes of the much higher rate of propagation of the negative discharge channel. The theoretical considerations are compared with the results of original experiments with positive and negative discharges of the length up to 60 m. The solution is of a key importance for the analysis of the breakdown process such as very long sparks or the lightning.

articleTitle: On the behaviour of insulations with interfaces voltage cable accessories-model investigations
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Electrical insulation systems for medium and for high-voltage cable terminations often contain several electrically stressed macroscopic interfaces. In the case of high-voltage insulators a chemical bondage between the different insulating materials is necessary to protect the interfaces against breakdown. For medium voltage cable accessories it is possible to use interfaces without a chemical bonding between the two interface partners. In this case the required insulating ability can also be achieved by means of the interface pressure of a stretched elastic insulating material. To evaluate the reliability of such interfaces the influences of the electrode distance d, the interface pressure p and the roughness R, of a plastic interface partner as well as the effect of a lubrication agent have been investigated. Additional measurements have been done to evaluate the long term behaviour of the interfaces.

articleTitle: Flashover to a resin bonded carbon fibre fishing rod from an overhead power line: doubt about the mechanism
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The question is raised whether breakdown to a carbon fibre fishing rod held a few metres from an overhead 33 kV power line might occur as the result of the discharge of accumulated charge on the rod arising from a rectifying action. The discharge might provoke muscular contraction in the person holding the rod so that the rod was sharply brought into contact with the energised conductors. Or perhaps the discharge might trigger long distance breakdown through the air.

articleTitle: Design, simulation and testing of an EHV metal-enclosed disconnector
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: One of the most demanding design issues in the development of metal-clad disconnecters for application at 500 kV and over, is to ensure the switching capabilities of the device. This paper presents the issues and processes involved from the initial design through to final testing of a 550 kV disconnector. The initial work concentrated on defining the design parameters in order to minimise the risk of are breakout. Computer analysis using 2D and 3D modelling of the contact configuration was carried out. As a following step, before building the disconnector, the results of the computations were validated by a static test where the electrode arrangement was set manually at different gap distances and discharges between contacts were monitored. From the computational and test data, a final contact design was optimised and a disconnector prototype was built. Finally the capabilities for bus-charging current switching were tested in accordance with the IEC 1259 standard. The results of these tests include measurement and comparison with EMTP simulations of the fast transient overvoltages generated by disconnector operations.

articleTitle: The effect of environmental factors on degradation and recovery characteristics of RTV silicone rubber
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Room temperature vulcanized (RTV) silicone rubber has been widely used to coat porcelain insulators to render water repellency to prevent formation of water filming on the surface and thus to suppress the leakage current and consequently flashover. However, the electrical property and its hydrophobicity of RTV silicone rubber coating under outdoor conditions may be influenced by many environmental factors. In this study various treatments, such as salt-fog, salt water immersion and UV irradiation were applied to the samples to investigate the change of the electrical property and hydrophobicity. As a result the leakage current increased and contact angle decreased as the degradation time is longer. But the degraded RTV silicone rubber has recovered its hydrophobicity during drying time in ambient condition because LMW (low molecular weight) silicone fluid diffused from the bulk to the surface.

articleTitle: Testing method and statistical analysis applied in lightning impulse critical flashover
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper presents software designed to deal statistically with the common lightning and switching testing results. The objective of the "Testing Method and Statistical Analysis" software is to make possible the fast analysis of the results of an impulse testing sequence, usually considering an amount of impulses per series much larger than the common practice. This software was designed to allow the automatic generation of reports, which makes the analysis of the results easy. It has the option of printing a complete report, recording of each test sequence results, setting up a complete historical data of the experiment with all the possible and available information, allowing the modification of any data to any moment, avoiding errors. By computing the critical flashover voltage, standard deviation paths and also the likelihood surface form, some analyses regarding the test execution can be performed.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of impulse creepage discharge in N/sub 2//SF/sub 6/ gas mixture
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: From the viewpoints of mitigation of global warming, technological strategies for the recycling and minimum consumption of SF/sub 6/ gas are under development. Alternative insulation gases and gas mixtures for SF/sub 6/ gas are promising in order to meet this problem. This paper describes the creepage discharge propagation characteristics and their mechanisms in N/sub 2//SF/sub 6/ gas mixtures for different mixture rate of SF/sub 6/ gas under positive lightning impulse voltage application. The authors simultaneously measured current and light intensity pulses and propagation speed of the creepage discharge. Experimental results revealed that the creepage discharge in gas mixtures propagated stepwise by the repetitive process of streamer propagation and streamer-leader transition. The streamer-leader transition time as well as the step length in gas mixtures approached to that in pure SF/sub 6/ gas by only 5% mixture of SF/sub 6/ gas.

publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering

articleTitle: Problems in the definition of magnetic field values to be measured on overhead power lines
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: From our field experience we have detected some problems on the definition of the measurement conditions for the magnetic field on transmission lines. In this paper the selection of the spatial component under measurement, the validity of the per unit current values, the selection of a lateral reference, the convenience of measurements at different lateral distances, the location of the measurement points respect the structures, and the position with respect to other electric lines are discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancing partial discharge measurement with extended resolution analyser
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Partial discharge fingerprints are generally obtained for model samples with known defects with computer-aided partial discharge analysers. These fingerprints help in generating a database for classification of PD defects. Due to differences in PD detector characteristics, the measurements can be different with different PD detectors. The fingerprints obtained then, are dependent on the characteristics of PD detectors and the fingerprints obtained may lead to wrong classification and interpretation. The paper proposes a solution of parallel detector scheme which will help obtain standard fingerprints independent of the PD detector characteristics.

articleTitle: SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/ mixtures for explosion-protected motors
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: With the aim to use SF/sub 6/-N/sub 2/ mixtures as purging and protective gases for explosion-protected machines, the PD inception voltage in the gas gaps of the end winding spaces was investigated. The PD was measured between two coils and between coils and earthed parts of the motor case for different pressures and SF/sub 6/ concentrations. The investigations focused on the electrical safety margin that could be reached with relatively small SF/sub 6/ admixtures. Conclusions have been drawn for the practical dimensioning of end winding spaces in high-voltage machines.

articleTitle: Experiences with stationary and mobile calibration laboratories
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Publication IEC 60060-2 recommends the requirements on the measuring equipment of high voltage laboratories. The operators of the laboratory have to assure that the measuring uncertainties stay within the prescribed limits. The inspections are preferably done by an accredited laboratory through comparison with a reference measuring system which is traceable to national standards. A high voltage calibration laboratory is illustrated, which can be operated either stationary in a high voltage laboratory or mobile on-site. The type of equipment and the necessary procedures for the performance checks and tests are described. The experiences after two years of operation are summarised. Moreover the operating costs and recalibration intervals are commented upon.

articleTitle: Improvement of electrical field analysis by use of computer aided software engineering (CASE) tools
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Field analysis of complex electrode configurations is an important task in the design of high-voltage apparatus or test-setups. Computer simulations in the design phase can reveal weaknesses and possible faults before expensive prototypes are built-up. Multi-purpose field analysis programs are available, providing graphical user interfaces (GUI) coupled with computer aided design (CAD) environments. Such integrated environments are still expensive and dependent on high-performance computer equipment. Most field analysis programs can be fed with scripts describing the problem to be investigated. This allows interpretation of the field analysis task as a software programming task. The matter of software programming is well known as software engineering (SE) and a large amount of strategies and computer tools exist that help to facilitate project management and to speed-up project schedules. Field analysis and software development are compared and similarities are revealed. With these similarities, commonly used strategies and tools from SE can be used to improve the model generation and calculation speed of field analysis. A review of SE strategies and tools shows that the benefit for the field analysis is a more effective handling of varied parameters, a significant reduction of calculation time and a robust model that allows easy maintenance. Although the finite element method (FEM) and a distinct analysis software were used, the principal ideas of SE here can be used with other field analysis methods and software programs.

articleTitle: Analysis of MOA location in substations
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper deals with simulation of lightning overvoltage generated by backflashes and direct strokes on a multiconductor model of real power lines, entering substations of various size and with various number of connected lines in range from 1 line up to 12 lines. Five real 400 kV substations are modelled as complete one phase schemes of busbars and all equipment connected. The simulation are repeated for various metal oxide arrester (MOA) locations including alternative without any protection. The resulting overvoltages in several basic points i.e. on line input with lightning, circuit breaker, busbar and power transformer are presented.

articleTitle: On-line monitoring instrument of fault discharge in large generators
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper describes a newly developed partial discharge (PD) on-line monitoring system used for large turbine generators. The system consists of a broadband current transducer, a computer-aided PD measurement system. By using a programmable fabricated band pass filter and an adaptive digital filter, the system can suppress the noise and extract PD signal from the intense noise surroundings successfully. At the end of this paper, some field test results, obtained from a 200 MW generating set, are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Overvoltages under asymmetrical condition on very high voltage overhead transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper presents a study regarding very high voltage overhead lines operating in asymmetrical conditions due to ground faults. The overvoltage factor is obtained by modeling the polyphase network with the mathematical apparatus of the theory of symmetrical components and with EMTP. For a single phase ground fault and reclosing on remanently charged line, a distinct influence is noted when modeling with and without consideration of the magnetization curve of the transformer, or considering corona discharge.

articleTitle: Software evaluation of step response parameters of high voltage dividers
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: High voltages are measured using a measuring system consisting of a high voltage divider, transmission system and recording instruments. These measuring equipment must to be calibrated periodically to have an accuracy within permissible limits. It involves determination of scale factor, linearity and its validity range with respect to signal parameters like frequency, amplitude and time parameters especially for impulse measuring systems. The time parameters can be determined by comparing the measuring system under test with another calibrated reference divider or by using a unit step generator. In this paper, different methods available to calibrate the high voltage measuring system such as methodology for voltage comparison method and dynamic response method are discussed. A software is also developed at CPRI to evaluate the divider time parameters such as base magnitude, settling level, virtual origin, overshoot /spl beta/, distortion time T/sub o/, partial response time T/sub /spl alpha//, experimental response time T/sub N/, residual response time T/sub R/, and settling time t/sub 5/. In order to check the validity of the software developed, international sample data for different step responses are considered. The response parameters of these data are compared with the response parameters evaluated by the software developed at CPRI. The paper describes the details of the algorithm and capabilities of the software.

articleTitle: Measurement of harmonics with optical sensor systems and investigation of harmonic sources in industrial distribution systems
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In this paper, using optical harmonic measuring instruments for high voltage and the harmonic analyzers, the patterns of the harmonics in the distribution systems in an industrial area were simultaneously measured at the field test location distribution line in the neighborhood of a factory and at the same distributing substation. Carrying out the measurements of harmonics in a communication factory and the method of phase discrimination, the authors have found the harmonic sources in an industrial distribution line. The power factor in an industrial distribution line was measured and evaluated by the distortion factor.

articleTitle: Dependence of dielectric loss factor, resistivity and parameters characterizing partial discharges on porcelain porosity
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The article presents research results of partial discharges, the dielectric loss factor and volume resistivity of porcelain of different porosity. Different porosity of porcelain was obtained by changing its firing temperature.

articleTitle: Influence of the degree of parallel partial discharges on the degradation of the insulation material
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In order to assess the aging state of complex insulation systems it is necessary to understand the intricate aging processes occuring in the insulation. Test objects out of epoxy resin with different degrees of parallel discharges are produced in order to determine the relation between the degree of parallel discharges and the degradation of insulation material. The damaging effect of the PD is proved by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and roughness measurements. A model based on simulation of the relevant gas discharge processes is used to interpret the results.

articleTitle: On-site testing of gas insulated substation with AC voltage
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Experience has proven that the reliability of a GIS/GIL can be ensured by an on-site AC-testing after assembly combined with a sensitive partial discharge measurement. Either conventional 50/60 Hz transformer systems or resonant test systems with variable inductance as well as resonant test systems with variable frequency have been used to perform the GIS/GIL on-site testing. The paper describes the different HV test systems with their advantages and limitations and the applicable partial discharge measuring methods. The UHF PD measuring method is emphasised.

articleTitle: Effective ionization coefficient of nitrogen including metastable molecules
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The authors have studied the mechanism of current variation with time for a negative point to plane corona gap in nitrogen rich condition. It has been deduced that the variation depends on density of metastable molecules of nitrogen. Those molecules have high potential energy and long life time. Thus, it may affect a magnitude of ionization coefficient: /spl alpha//sub eff/. In this report, a magnitude of /spl alpha//sub eff/ of nitrogen including metastable molecules was measured. From the results, its value increased with density of metastable molecules.

articleTitle: Breakdown characteristics of CO/sub 2/ containing 0.125% of SF/sub 6/
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: AC breakdown strengths of CO/sub 2/, SF/sub 6/ and a mixture of CO/sub 2/+SF/sub 6/ containing 0.125% of SF/sub 6/ in nonuniform field were experimentally studied. The electrode gap spacing and the relative gas pressure were varied within the range of 5-25 mm and of 100-500 kPa respectively. The experimental results have shown that the addition of SF/sub 6/ to CO/sub 2/ causes a significant increase of the AC breakdown voltage with respect to CO/sub 2/. Even at about pressures of 300 kPa and 25 mm gap spacing breakdown voltage of mixture were obtained 15% higher than that of pure SF/sub 6/ and 54% higher than that of pure CO/sub 2/.

articleTitle: Design and development of an adaptable gas insulated bushing
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper describes the methodology adopted for the design and development of a gas insulated bushing, made of composite or synthetic insulator housing. A noteworthy feature of the design is the adaptability of the bushing, to suit an already developed cone insulator for 145 kV class gas insulated switchgear. Based on detailed analytical studies for electric field distribution, the internal electrical design for the bushing has been carried out. The various components like central conductor, stress relief shield, current collector and current transfer arrangement have been fabricated. The prototype has successfully withstood the dielectric tests as per specifications.

articleTitle: A high voltage calibration method using the measuring spark gap
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Spark gap use as a measuring system is still accepted by the international standards, in certain cases being an alternative for measuring circuit calibration. High voltage (HV) measurement is based on the experimental results of the calibrations carried out by several international laboratories and on the knowledge of correction factors corresponding to the atmospheric conditions during the test. The paper presents an updating of the process for atmospheric conditions measurement and for automatic determination of the spacing necessary to calibrate a voltage by means of the spark gap. Using the least squares method the analytical expression was determined under the form of interpolating polynomials for different voltage and sphere diameter types.

articleTitle: Contact area at the interface between a discharge and an electrolytic solution
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In order to simulate the propagation characteristics of a local discharge on an electrolytic solution under an impulse voltage application, it is necessary to know the contact area at the interface between the discharge and the solution surface and the electric field distribution along the surface. In this study, a calculation method of the contact area is proposed. The outline of the area was assumed a circle and its radius was calculated from the applied voltage, electrode-fall, current density at the interface and the resistance of the solution part. The calculation results agreed with the values estimated from the Schlieren photographs reported before. Furthermore, the potential distribution along the surface was obtained using the calculated radius.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the streamer guiding field in SF/sub 6/ under positive and negative polarity
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: In spite of the great number of studies, there is a disagreement to the existence and consequently to the value of the electric field in the streamer channel in SF/sub 6/. In this paper, three experimental methods are proposed to determinate the streamer guiding field under positive and negative polarity. The considerable amount of experimental data leads to the conclusion that the value of the streamer guiding field (average geometrical field in the corona region) under positive and negative polarity, is about 40 kVcm/sup -1/ at atmospheric pressure. This result is very important for a great number of industrial applications using SF/sub 6/.

articleTitle: Study on mechanisms and propagation characteristics of partial discharges in SF/sub 6/ GIS
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: It is imperative to study partial discharge behavior in SF/sub 6/ GIS in order to carry out reliable insulation diagnosis and conditioning evaluation of practical gas-insulated systems. This paper deals with investigation on propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves owing to partial discharges in a SF/sub 6/ GIS model as well as the PD mechanisms, by utilizing various electrical measuring and optical detecting techniques. Leader discharges prior to breakdown can be readily discriminated and the attenuation characteristics of electromagnetic waves within the GIS has been established. A suggestion is also put forward to set up a comprehensive PD detection and insulation performance evaluation system for reliable and efficient application to practical GIS.

articleTitle: The influence of floating electrodes in the results of impulse tests
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: When testing high voltage set-ups for searching for the critical flashover voltage the value of the associated standard deviation, as stated in technical standards, is usually assumed as lower than 3%. Normally, high values of standard deviation indicate problems in the accomplishment of the test. This work deals with the influence of floating electrodes close to the region of the formation of the electrical field on the values of standard deviation of the critical flashover. The presented results are based in tests carried out in a 15 kV spacer system and in rod-rod gaps.

articleTitle: Application of P and MP algorithms to high voltage digital measurements
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper applies the Prony and matrix pencil (P & MP) algorithms to high voltage digital measurements for the first time. In these algorithms, the measured data are fitted by a linear combination of complex exponentials. Therefore they are quite applicable to signal processing in digital measurements of high voltage and other electrical engineering.

articleTitle: Application of generalised characteristics of the corona discharge in forecasts of environmental impact of bipolar HVDC lines
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The paper reports generalised experimental volt-ampere characteristics of unipolar corona for a conductor inside a coaxial cylinder and above a plane, as well as for a bipolar system of conductors. Relationships between the generalised characteristics permit a tentative reduction of the corona current system to a unipolar current inside a coaxial cylinder, for which the current density and the electric field strength, essential for environmental assessment of bipolar HVDC power transmission lines, can be easily calculated.

articleTitle: Influence of manufacturing parameters on the PD-behaviour of AlN-substrates
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: Metallized aluminiumnitride-substrates (AlN) for power semiconductor modules are examined in regard to their partial discharge behaviour. The samples used differ in the size of the metallization and in the duration of the structuring etching process, which has an effect on the vertical geometry of the edges. Other examined samples were metallized by sputtering a thin layer of copper onto the surface of a blank AlN-plate instead of the usual bond technology. These samples differ in size and shape of the metallization. It is found out that the duration of the etching process has a decreasing influence on the appearance of partial discharges of high apparent charge. This is because a longer etching process makes the edges of the metallization become steeper and some thin copper on the surface of the ceramic along the edges disappear. As in these examinations sets of samples with different sizes of the metallization are regarded the desired effect can be seen in each set of samples. When comparing the sets to each other, an influence of the size of the metallization on the PD-behaviour with bigger samples showing more PD can be recognized. This is proved by PD-measurements of the samples with sputtered metallization. In regard to the shapes of the metallization the influence of the angles of a corner is examined. It can be seen that smaller angles cause more partial discharge because of higher field strength at the tip.

articleTitle: Consequences of the degradation of the cathode and of the anode on breakdown voltage value in compressed SF/sub 6/
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: This paper deals with the electrode erosion because roughness produced by high current is one of the most important factors affecting dielectric performance in spark gaps. The large reduction of the threshold for breakdown in compressed SF/sub 6/ is studied taking the degradation of the anode and of the cathode into account.

articleTitle: Calibration of a 3 MV LI measuring system by comparison method and by numerical convolution using its measured step response
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: The dynamic errors of peak value u/spl circ/, front time T/sub 1/ and time to half value T/sub 2/ of an approved 3 MV LI (lightning impulse) measuring system were experimentally determined for two standard LIs with u/spl circ/=500 kV, T/sub 1/=1.2 /spl mu/s/spl plusmn/20% and T/sub 2/=60 /spl mu/s by two different methods. The first method is according to the comparison of an Approved Measuring System with a 500 kV Reference Measuring System. The second method is the convolution of the normalized step response g(t) of the 3 MV system with the standard LI input voltage measured with the Reference Measuring System. Agreement within 0.5% for u/spl circ/ and within 1.2% for T/sub 1/ and T/sub 2/ was achieved.

articleTitle: Measurement of overhead line electrical clearances of importance to the safety of persons
publicationTitle: 1999 Eleventh International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering
abstract: There are currently no international standards for the determination of withstand distances to ensure safety of personnel from power lines during their normal operation. The safety distances that are used within each country are generally specified in a deterministic manner by the utilities themselves or by their trade association. Experience has proved these safety distances to be adequate. The distances to be used in live line working have been considered by the IEC and a standard has been issued on the method of calculation. This standard uses the latest information from IEC 71 (on insulation co-ordination) and includes knowledge for Cigre WG 33-07. It is recognised by IEC TC 11 that there is a need for an international standard to determine electrical safety distances. The method is consistent with the IEC method for the determination of the Live Line Minimum Approach Distances and a Committee Draft (reference number 11/138/CD) has been circulated for national comments. The approach taken in this Committee Draft is similar to that of the live line document, but recognises that additional overvoltages on the power system can occur (in particular overvoltages associated with lightning and circuit energisation and reenergisation). The work described here is supportive of the approach being taken by the IEC TC 11 Project and the work of Cenelec TC 11. The U/sub 50/ values and standard deviations of a number of key configurations have been measured.
